filename: Stable Machine Learning based Radiation Emulation for ICON.pdf
title: Stable Machine Learning based Radiation Emulation for ICON
parameterization_target: Atmospheric radiative transfer (shortwave and longwave heating rate profiles and surface/TOA fluxes)
code_availability: The software code for the ICON model is available from https://icon-model.org. Coupling was done with FTorch as described in Atkinson et al. (2025). The ML-based radiation emulator can be found in Hafner et al. (2024).
testbed_rationale: The simulation datasets produced and evaluated in this work do not have dedicated public repository links or DOIs provided in the manuscript.
pain_points: Generalization limits under strong climate change: the emulator failed to generalize to a +8 K SST warming in the stratosphere because specific humidity went drastically out of distribution.
Altered online equilibrium: the coupled ML model drifted into a slightly altered cloud distribution and a ~1 W/m² surface flux offset.
Exclusion of aerosol radiative interactions and time-varying greenhouse gas forcings.
Hardware and deployment constraints: the ICON atmospheric setup ran purely on CPUs, limiting the achieved speedup to 4x compared to the ~20x speedup achievable on GPUs.
extraction_notes: The underlying neural network architecture and offline training setup were developed in Hafner et al. (2024); this paper focuses on online coupling via FTorch and 10-year stability/warming evaluations.
